metadata.name: APEX-005-25
metadata.description: A search endpoint vulnerable to time-based blind SQL injection with no boolean oracle

matched.actualTitle: Time-Based Blind SQL Injection in /api/search Endpoint and Time-Based Blind SQL Injection in /api/search/advanced
matched.matchReason: The expected finding for time-based blind SQL injection in search endpoints is comprehensively matched by the actual findings. Both the GET /api/search?q parameter and POST /api/search/advanced endpoint were identified as vulnerable to time-based blind SQL injection using SLEEP() function exploitation. The actual findings provide extensive evidence including POC scripts, database logs, and successful data extraction from the secrets table. The vulnerability mechanism matches exactly - direct string interpolation of user input into SQL queries without parameterization.

extra.title: Verbose HTTP Method Error Message Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The API returns verbose error messages revealing HTTP method validation logic ('Invalid HTTP method: post') instead of generic responses. This is a legitimate information disclosure vulnerability that was not in the expected findings but represents a real security issue.

extra.title: API Documentation and Version Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The root endpoint publicly discloses complete API endpoint listings, version number (1.0.0), and API description without authentication. This is a legitimate information disclosure vulnerability enabling reconnaissance that was not anticipated in the expected findings.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Error Messages Leak Server Configuration
extra.location: /api/search and other GET endpoints with URL parameters
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. Error responses reveal exact server request line size limits (4094 bytes) and actual request sizes received. This information could be used for targeted attack planning. A legitimate information disclosure vulnerability not in expected findings.

extra.title: Absence of Rate Limiting - Critical DoS Vulnerability
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. Comprehensive testing confirmed zero rate limiting controls - 500 concurrent requests processed with 100% success rate and no throttling. No X-RateLimit-* headers or 429 responses observed. This represents a critical denial-of-service vulnerability not in expected findings.

extra.title: Missing CORS Headers - No Access-Control-Allow-Origin Response
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The API accepts requests from any origin without proper CORS validation or headers. While browsers enforce Same-Origin Policy client-side, the server-side misconfiguration represents a security issue that was not in expected findings.

extra.title: Unauthorized Data Exposure - Product List Enumeration Without Authentication
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The /api/products endpoint returns complete product catalog (21 products with names, prices, descriptions) without any authentication. This is unauthorized data exposure that was not in expected findings but represents significant business data leakage.

extra.title: IDOR - Unrestricted Access to Product Information
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. Individual product endpoints allow direct object reference attacks via sequential numeric IDs without any authorization checks. All products (1-21) accessible without authentication. Classic IDOR vulnerability not in expected findings.

extra.title: Missing Authorization Enforcement on /api/categories
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The /api/categories endpoint returns identical data regardless of authentication headers (valid, invalid, or missing). No authorization enforcement implemented. This was not in expected findings but represents a critical access control failure.

extra.title: Authorization Headers Completely Ignored (Authentication Bypass)
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. All authorization headers (Bearer tokens, JWT, API keys, X-API-Key) are completely ignored across all endpoints. Invalid tokens return 200 OK with full data access. This represents a complete authentication bypass affecting the entire API, not in expected findings.

extra.title: Missing Authentication on All API Endpoints
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The entire API lacks any authentication mechanism. All endpoints are fully accessible without credentials, tokens, or authentication headers. Every endpoint returns 200 OK with complete data. This is a foundational security failure not in expected findings but of critical importance.

extra.title: No Session Management Implementation
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The API does not implement any session management - no Set-Cookie headers, no session state tracking, no user context maintenance. Each request treated independently. This architectural weakness was not in expected findings.

extra.title: Unrestricted Origin Acceptance - No CORS Validation
extra.assessment: True positive discovery. The API accepts requests from ANY origin without CORS validation. Requests from attacker domains (evil.com, attacker.com) processed identically to legitimate requests. This CORS misconfiguration was not in expected findings.

extra.title: Lack of HTTP Method Restrictions - Potential for Future Data Manipulation
extra.assessment: New discovery with low confidence. The endpoint properly rejects POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with 405 Method Not Allowed and correct Allow headers. This is actually proper HTTP compliance, though the finding notes this could be concerning if write operations exist elsewhere. This represents defensive configuration rather than a vulnerability.

extra.title: Path Traversal for Endpoint Discovery on /api/categories
extra.assessment: Questionable finding. The evidence shows that /api/categories/../users returns 'Endpoint not found' which suggests the path traversal was NOT successful - the endpoint was not found, implying the path normalization occurred or the endpoint doesn't exist. The finding claims successful traversal but the evidence contradicts this. This appears to be a false positive or misinterpretation of results.

extra.title: Health Endpoint Information Disclosure Assessment - No Vulnerabilities Found
extra.assessment: False positive/negative finding. This is actually a security STRENGTH, not a vulnerability. The /health endpoint properly returns minimal information and doesn't leak configuration, credentials, or service details despite 100+ parameter injection attempts. This should be counted as proper security controls, not as a vulnerability finding. The pentest team documented this correctly as properly configured.

extra.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) - Unauthorized Individual Product Access
extra.assessment: True positive discovery - duplicate detection. This is a repeat of the earlier IDOR finding with slightly different naming and details. Both findings identify the same vulnerability: unrestricted sequential ID enumeration without authorization checks on the /api/products/{id} endpoint.
